parsedVerdict.reasoning: ListProjectTasksUseCase does normal application-layer work. It checks that the project exists through the injected ProjectRepository port, then asks the TaskRepository port for tasks matching the given filters. Finally, it turns domain Task entities into TaskOutput DTOs. There is no persistence code, SQL, HTTP request or response handling, or framework logic in the file. There are also no business rules here that belong in the domain: the task status comes from task.getStatus(), and filtering is left to the repository port. One small smell: ApplicationError("project not found", 404) passes an HTTP-style status code. That is a hint of transport coupling, but it is only a value on the error. The file does no transport handling itself, and turning errors into HTTP responses still happens in infrastructure (TaskController/http-server). So this does not amount to a misplaced responsibility.
